title: Hemocytometer cell count and trypan-blue viability
summary: Prepare a synthetic cell suspension, load two hemocytometer chambers, apply a consistent boundary rule, and calculate viable-cell concentration, viability and counting uncertainty.
scenario: A synthetic, non-human suspension culture needs a viable-cell count before its next simulated passage. Each displayed chamber represents one 1 mm × 1 mm square at 0.1 mm depth: 0.0001 mL. Use equal sample and trypan-blue volumes for a twofold dilution. This is a synthetic field, not a microscope image or a diagnostic specimen.
guided_steps: Mix the suspension for at least 5 seconds before sampling.
Mix 10 µL cell suspension with 10 µL trypan blue. The dilution factor is (10 + 10)/10 = 2.
Seat the coverslip, then load chambers A and B separately by capillary action.

For every visible cell choose unstained, stained, or exclude. Include cells touching the top or left outer boundary; exclude cells touching the bottom or right. Classify included cells by their displayed stain.
Record each chamber's included unstained and stained tallies. Excluded cells do not enter either tally.
Viable cells/mL = (total included unstained cells / 2 chambers) × 10,000 × dilution factor.
Viability = included unstained / all included cells × 100. Poisson relative counting uncertainty = 100/√(all included cells) percent; it does not include preparation errors.
Submit the calculations for a formative debrief.

checkpoints.description: Resuspend the synthetic cells before sampling.
checkpoints.rationale: Settling makes an aliquot unrepresentative of the suspension.

checkpoints.description: Prepare and account for the twofold sample-plus-dye dilution.
checkpoints.rationale: The original concentration must be corrected for added dye volume.

checkpoints.description: Seat the coverslip before loading either chamber.
checkpoints.rationale: The chamber geometry and capillary fill depend on the seated coverslip.

checkpoints.description: Record independent tallies for both chambers.
checkpoints.rationale: Two fields provide a simple check on loading and counting variation.

checkpoints.description: Keep each displayed field within the exercise's countable range.
checkpoints.rationale: Very sparse counts have large relative sampling uncertainty; crowded fields are difficult to classify.

checkpoints.description: Apply the top/left inclusion and bottom/right exclusion rule with correct stain classifications.
checkpoints.rationale: A consistent rule prevents double-counting or omitting boundary cells; stain and boundary decisions are distinct.

checkpoints.description: Calculate viable-cell concentration from the learner's included unstained tally, chamber volume and dilution.
checkpoints.rationale: Concentration = mean included unstained count / chamber volume × dilution factor.

source.note: The calculation uses the declared 0.0001 mL chamber volume.

checkpoints.description: Calculate the percentage of included cells that are unstained.
checkpoints.rationale: In this synthetic model, unstained cells represent membrane-intact viable cells and stained cells non-viable cells.

source.note: Trypan-blue exclusion is a model of membrane integrity, not a universal measure of cell health.

checkpoints.description: Estimate relative Poisson counting uncertainty from all included cells.
checkpoints.rationale: For an ideal Poisson count N, standard deviation √N gives relative uncertainty 100/√N percent.

source.note: This approximation excludes mixing, dilution, loading and classification bias.

sources.use: Appendix H pp. 466–468: cell-culture work requires a risk assessment of material source, cell type, culture type and procedure; human and other primate cells need BSL-2 practices at a minimum. This synthetic non-human exercise does not establish human-cell handling competency.

limitations: All cells, fields and results are synthetic. No real specimen, culture, stain or microscope is used.
The field is a two-dimensional counting diagram, not a microscope image; it cannot train focus, morphology recognition, aseptic handling or pipetting technique.
The top/left rule is this exercise's convention. Follow the actual chamber and laboratory procedure; equivalent consistent boundary conventions exist.
Trypan-blue exclusion models membrane integrity only. It does not establish future growth, phenotype, sterility or overall cell health.
Poisson uncertainty describes ideal counting variation only, not total measurement uncertainty or biological variability.

This is an unreviewed layer-2 protocol pilot, not the complete cell-culture course or a safety/competency qualification. Human and primate cells require a separate risk assessment and institutional procedures.
